phase3_findings.description: run_memory_call (src/sqllens/memory/store.py 88-99) attaches nothing to the concurrent future; when the awaiting task is cancelled after the store call starts, asyncio drops the worker's result or exception and nothing logs it. A failing delete_memory / clear_memories / import_memory baseline (clear=True) call whose caller was cancelled loses its error (handler logger.exception at server.py 599-603, 623-627 already unwound with CancelledError), and a successful delete or wipe leaves no log line. Regression versus the on-loop design; the SQL pool's precedent is sql_threads.py 119-122, 157 (future.add_done_callback(_log_call_after_cancel)). Tests cover only ordering of a cancelled delete, not its outcome.

One worker with an unbounded queue: a hung ChromaDB call stalls every later memory tool call forever with no timeout, no caller error and no log line; transport.md line 121 documents the trade-off, but the SQL pool warns on saturation and times out slot waits.
A nested run_memory_call from code already on the memory worker deadlocks silently; only the docstring (store.py 95-96) guards it, with no thread check or error. No current path reaches it.

The no-overlap / off-loop invariant is held only by call sites (server.py 542, 566, 591, 620, 695, 729; importer.py 76) and tests, not by MemoryStore: its synchronous methods, the memory.admin functions and exporter.py 41/47 stay directly callable from the loop; the no-reentry rule is prose only.

store.py 70-73 comment (and docs/internal/mcp-server/transport.md line 34) claims the single worker protects ChromaAgentMemory's lazy unlocked client/collection creation, but ChromaAgentMemory's own two-thread executor (agent_memory.py 135-175; _save, _delete, _clear, searches) also calls those and can overlap the memory worker. Not a regression.
